text: Bribe the Great Scholar
Not every Cathayan is a loyal minister and able general — with sufficient reward, a great scholar can always be found to argue your case.
Reclaim Wei Jing
You have reclaimed Wei Jing from foreign hands!
Appeasement and Self-Preservation
Troubles within your own domain leave you no time to spare — you have no heart to march at once to retake Wei Jing.
Other Cathayan factions will declare war on them
All Cathayan factions loyal to the Dragon Emperor will jointly declare war on the foreign invaders who seized Wei Jing
You cannot make peace with Cathayan factions while you control Wei Jing
You will face Cathayan forces on the battlefield
Cathay's wrath shall never cease until the capital is reclaimed!
Through your efforts, Wei Jing has finally returned to Cathay's embrace. Your name shall be recorded in history as a hero for the ages!
Wei Jing has been liberated by another Cathayan faction!
Wei Jing has been seized by another foreign power. Cathay may now make peace with the original faction
All-Out War
Bribe the Grand Scholar
Force a declaration of war against the Zhen Dan faction, unable to make peace with them while controlling Wei Jing
Foster friendly relations with Zhen Dan

Wei Jing, the pearl atop the Celestial Empire's crown, home to the Five Elements Compass and the Dragon Emperor's palace among mortals. This greatest of imperial capitals now lies in our hands, but it is only a matter of time before the people of Zhen Dan mount a ferocious counterattack...
The Fall of Wei Jing
Agree to Join the War
Appease and Hold Fast
Zhen Dan's fury shall never subside until the capital is retaken!
Wei Jing? What is that to me?

Wei Jing, the pearl atop the Celestial Empire's crown, home to the Five Elements Compass and the Dragon Emperor's palace among mortals. This greatest of imperial capitals has now fallen to a foreign race — a disgrace to all of Zhen Dan! Messengers from the God-Strategy Bureau have already been dispatched across the land, the princes and nobles of every court stand ready with weapons in hand, and armies from all directions are converging upon the capital\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Let those not of our people who hold the capital know: the whole world shall strike as one![[/col]]
Wei Jing Lost
The Fall of Wei Jing
Wei Jing Changes Hands
Reclaim Wei Jing
Reclaim Wei Jing
Aid the Realm in Crisis
Zhen Dan's Shame
Wei Jing has been captured by a foreign faction
Wei Jing has changed hands among foreign factions time and again, yet Zhen Dan remains powerless to act. This shall be an eternal disgrace...
Urgent news from the front! Word has come that one of the allied provincial armies has successfully retaken Wei Jing—the capital has returned to Zhen Dan's embrace!

As golden blades shattered Wei Jing's weathered southern gate, an eerie silence drifted among the crumbling ruins and broken walls. The remaining glazed tiles on the flying eaves gleamed blood-red in the twilight, and the white marble pillars once inscribed with 'Celestial Empire Above All' were now scarred with the cracks of foreign blades\\n\\nFirst came a decaying vermilion door, its ruined hinges shrieking. An aged face emerged from within, withered fingers clutching desperately at the doorframe, clouded pupils trembling violently the moment they recognized the Zhen Dan banners. 'The royal army, the royal army has arrived!' The hoarse cry of a lame old scholar broke the deathly stillness. Rustling footsteps gradually rose upon the flagstone road, faint as silkworms nibbling leaves at first, then surging like crashing waves. Ragged refugees crawled from the rubble; a scholar with severed fingers clutched half a scroll of poetry and wept upon his knees; a noblewoman with disheveled hair and bare feet bowed thrice and kowtowed nine times toward the palace. As your army marched past the bronze dragon-head statues before the Heavenly Gate, the sobs of countless thousands had already turned into thunderous cheers that shook heaven and earth\\n\\nThe crimson sunset, like blood, melted the frost clinging to your war robes. The dragon banner rose once more atop Wei Jing's walls, fluttering in the wind. The arrows lodged deep in the city walls, the tattered banners drifting through the markets, the scholar's caps hanging from withered trees—all now trembled softly in the breeze. The bell of the Heavenly Gate tolled, and with it, your name echoed throughout Wei Jing
You will join the other Zhen Dan factions in declaring war on the faction that seized Wei Jing, and cannot make peace with them until the capital is reclaimed
A Zhen Dan faction has declared war on you, swearing to wash away the disgrace of Wei Jing with your blood
The World Strikes as One
Cathay shall wash away the shame brought upon Wei Jing with the blood of the invaders!
[[col:red]]Panic Spreads (Turns 1-8 after the capital's fall)[[/col]]

To the people of Cathay, Wei Jing is not merely the capital, but a symbol of the bond between the mortal world and the Dragon Emperor and Moon Empress — an immortal and mysterious Celestial Court. When word of its fall reaches their ears, every Cathayan feels a dread and fury welling up from the heart.
[[col:red]]Chaos Looms (Turns 8-16 after the capital's fall)[[/col]]

Wei Jing still remains in the hands of the foreign enemy. The defeated generals cast blame upon one another, yet none dares lead troops to attack, and the plan to reclaim the lost territory has nearly run aground. Though the allied armies of Cathay still eye the occupying forces in the capital with hostile intent, as the center of power over the realm has fallen, the lords harboring their own ambitions have already begun scheming for themselves...
[[col:red]]The Celestial Empire's Collapse (16 turns after the capital's fall)[[/col]]

The armies of Cathay have lost the will to reclaim the lost lands. Lords harboring treacherous intent openly swallow up each other's jurisdictions, the helpless commonfolk are scattered and displaced, and the collapse of the Celestial Empire draws ever nearer. In so vast an empire, is there truly no one who can lead us to turn the tide?
Strife Within the Walls

The tiered palaces of Wei Jing show a swath of crimson beneath the dying sun, and suspicion among those who hold the game pieces has grown hard to suppress. No dragon shadow is seen at the Celestial Court, yet Yuan Bo stumbles about among the rainforests, blind to the chaos gripping the realm; the Palace Guard turns away the Jade Court's envoys at the gates, while the generals of the God-Strategy Bureau campaign across the four directions like unbridled wild horses. The Ravenfolk have poured out of Shang Wu in full force, and the carved bronze locks of ornate offices crack one by one in the gathering dusk, as vermilion-sealed dispatches fall like snow into the incinerators.\\nThough two deeply cautious leaders still maintain a precarious balance atop the Celestial Court, beneath this consensus thin as cicada wings, the tablets of the Nine Ministers have already quietly shifted. Rivalry has taken root, and dusk draws near. As a triangular crossbow bolt fletched in azure feathers pierces the throat of a Jade Court messenger, the fine rain smears the last line of vermilion annotation on the manifesto nailed to the God-Strategy Bureau's gate: "In the year of Bing Chen, at the White Dew, the star of calamity hangs over the capital."
We should support the Dragon-Kin
Zhen Dan's millennium-long grand enterprise rests upon his shoulders. Yuan Bo will be glad to see his old colleague still choose to trust him
I fear Yun Xiang is more reliable
Yun Xiang has seen problems that the lofty dragon-kin have overlooked, and would be pleased to see a meritorious hero of Zhen Dan willing to stand shoulder to shoulder with him
Attempt to Mediate

With a great enemy at the gates, Zhen Dan cannot afford internal strife. As one of Zhen Dan's pillar figures, your proposal cannot be ignored by anyone. Convene a meeting - perhaps we can turn back this crisis of infighting
Perhaps we should wait and see
That internal turmoil stirred up by petty schemers still lingers fresh in memory, but now is not the time to intervene. The Celestial Dynasty's two great ministers know their own measure
Diplomatic Stance: %+n with Celestial Loyalists
Diplomatic Stance: %+n with the Jade Court
Will trigger subsequent events.
A Meeting of Man and Dragon

You have succeeded in persuading both Yun Xiang and Yuan Bo to attend the meeting, but the atmosphere in the hall bodes ill—the Dragon Emperor's Guard and the Jade Court's Decree Guard glare at one another, Yun Xiang's displeasure toward Yu Long is written plain across his brow, while Yuan Bo makes no secret of his utter disregard for this undying "commoner." We need an issue that can unite them in common purpose.
Urge both to consider the people of Cathay
Whatever their differences, both of them act to protect Zhen Dan. On this matter, perhaps they can reach an agreement
Remind them the great enemies of the Celestial Empire have already descended
Zhen Dan already treads on thin ice, and the threat from the forces of Destruction has never been more menacing. Infighting will bring ruin to the Celestial Dynasty in an instant
Point out that blockade and infiltration are tearing Cathay apart

The Ravens and the Hong Wu Overseers have poured energy meant for fighting foreign enemies into pointless mutual attrition. Zhen Dan's intelligence network crumbles under their mutual blockades, and the rivalry between the Jade Court and the God-Strategy Bureau will ultimately backfire
Seal off the assembly and incite rebellion

Everyone present was stunned - no one had expected that one of Zhen Dan's trusted pillars would stir up a rebellion in the very midst of this council. Without doubt, you have succeeded in uniting Zhen Dan's various factions, but now they will turn against you
You support the Jade Court, and the Jade Court will surely repay you.
Return Gift from the Jade Court
The God-Strategy Bureau holds the military authority of Zhen Dan, and it will naturally reward those who help them.
Aid from the God-Strategy Bureau

The common people are forever the foundation of Zhen Dan. No one can deny this, and even Dragon-kin and champions of the Dragon Gods will be reduced to dust in history if they continue to disregard the multitudes.
Peaceful Living and Contentment
Zhen Dan has come to a moment of life and death. The forces of destruction are knocking at the gates of the Celestial Empire. We must set aside our disputes and face the enemy together.
Sharpening Spears, Feeding Horses
The Raven Guard and the Hong Wu Overseers should be sent where they are truly needed, to serve as the eyes and ears of Zhen Dan, not to blind one another.
Seamless as a Heavenly Robe
All of Zhen Dan will become our enemy, but the arrow has left the bow. Civil war has come.
Great Rebellion
Gain substantial bonuses, but all loyalist factions will become hostile towards you.
Envoy from the Vast Heavens

Violent thunder shakes your camp, and an unexpected visitor leaves your soldiers pale with shock: a member of the Dragon Emperor's Guard. The last time they left the capital was during the era of internal strife—these greatest warriors of the Celestial Dynasty were sent to strip generals of their authority across the land, crushing any who defied their orders like ants underfoot. That our power today stands unmatched in a hundred years makes their appearance here no good omen; this may be a test from the Celestial Court, or perhaps, a judgment.\\n\\nThe breath leaking from behind the guard's gilded mask sets the Dipper banner before the central tent fluttering ceaselessly, and the air congeals with cold. The instant the dragon-scale gold studs on his boot soles grind across the tent's threshold, you hear the sound of twenty-eight staff officers dropping to their knees behind you, the jade beads on their swords trembling with their masters' shivers—much like the twitching throats of the princes and lords once stripped of their tallies of command.
Treat Them with Courtesy

The Imperial Guard delivers the Dragon Emperor's grace and favor unto you. The Astronomical Bureau's scribe records with trembling hands: this is the one hundred and eighth time Hao Tian has traced out the meaning of 'loyalty' in the mortal world
Display Your Majesty

Behind the gilded face-mask, his eyes betray a fleeting flash of surprise, golden ripples stirring in the depths of the Imperial Guard's pupils. He raises a finger to tap lightly against his Hao Tian halberd, and tongues of fire bloom like lotus blossoms beneath the dragon-head hilt - the unique warning sign of the Dragon Emperor's Guard, beneath whose resonant hum thirty-six rebel kings once lost their heads. A scroll of gilded dragon-scale decree unfurls from the guard's hand - the scales themselves seem to pulse slowly, ancient seal-script burning within the tent: 'By the witness of mountains and rivers, the Imperial banner is bestowed upon thee'
The Great Tides of the World

Wisps of smoke curl from the bronze censer, and the ministers' arguments stir the light and shadow across the Celestial Dynasty's map like muddied water. The Minister of War slams his gilded, silver-inlaid ceremonial sword against the edge of the sand table, startling the jade pieces marking the capital region into a tremble. "Since the great campaign of Wei Jing, my lord's achievements—opening the canals, pacifying the vassal garrisons, breaking the invading enemy—have long eclipsed those who merely play the ape wearing a cap upon the throne of the Celestial Palace!" His fingertips sweep across the mottled sword-marks on the sand table, and the lacquered pieces of fifteen provinces topple at once. "This humble officer dares to speak: His Sagely Majesty has sat sealed away in the capital for a hundred years, and still the blade is held backwards by its hilt—court and country alike harbor their own hidden agendas. If we do not act with extraordinary measures now..."\\n\\nBefore he finishes, the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, clad in a crane-feather cloak, suddenly hurls the jade tablet from his robes. The green jade from Hotan cracks against the table with a sharp report. "Does the Minister mean to teach our lord to overturn the realm and its altars?" His slender hand sweeps across the cloud patterns on the screen. "Each dragon-blooded prince upholds His Majesty's rites, ruling their own domain, each fulfilling their own duty; now you would have him command the realm to set the world aright, yet the world knows only that he seeks to swallow fifteen provinces whole. Even should golden armor gleam beneath the sun, how could the common people ever submit their hearts?"\\n\\nAn east wind rolls back the curtain, revealing the Dragon Emperor's statue enshrined behind it, and the Grand Remonstrance Officer abruptly draws his blade and rises, its cold gleam sweeping across the Nine Provinces upon the map. "When the Prince of Nan Yang once coveted the throne, even he knew 'virtue matters more than the tripod'!" The blade's edge traces across the realm, then returns to its sheath. "Since the age of chaos began, is there a single commoner under heaven who does not know my lord's name? Should you act now, success or failure rests not with you, but with the ten thousand people. You have campaigned for years, and the people have watched your every move. If you act with sincerity to fulfill their hopes, then even overturning the old order, the realm may yet submit in awe; but if you act with cruelty and wanton pride, storing up the people's resentment, then even should you die in glory today, the historical records will still record your transgressions."\\n\\nWhatever is decided today, a new era has already arrived. The great river bursts its banks, and floodwaters mixed with cinnabar and clay sweep over the past, churning the gilded memorials of the old nobility into mud.
Endorse the Idea of Unifying the Provinces

The division of rule among the dragon-kin has fractured Zhen Dan's strength. As a unified whole, Zhen Dan would be far more powerful than its scattered provinces. In the end, they will unite beneath my banner
Recognize the Structure of Provinces Each Fulfilling Their Duties

Each dragon-kin fulfills their own duty, adapting to local circumstances - meeting soldiers with generals, water with earthworks - dividing and conquering the enemy on every side. Were I to obstinately force the provinces into unification, would that not be moving further from the goal while claiming to seek it?
The division of rule among the Dragons has fractured Zhen Dan's strength. A unified Zhen Dan would be far mightier than its scattered provinces - they will eventually unite under my banner.
Command Over All Six Directions

Each dragon holds their own duty, adapting to circumstance, meeting soldiers with generals and floods with earthworks, dividing and dissolving the threats on every side. If I insisted on unifying all provinces by my will alone, would that not be heading south while aiming for the north?
Each to Their Own Duty
A Blade Hidden in the Sleeve

The campfire in the hour of the Tiger is torn apart by the north wind. As you lift the tent flap, your Personal Guard commander's goose-feather sword is pressed against a Hong Wu Overseer—it seems what pillowed your sleep was not moonlight, but the blade of an enemy within. These spies, meant to serve as the Dragon Emperor's ears and eyes, are not as impeccable as the Onyx Ravenfolk: cold, merciless, and never treacherous.\\n\\nThe chains around the kneeling man's neck tremble with the dull thud of combat boots against the ground, and the short blade wrested from him still gleams with cold light—had your Personal Guard not been so alert, this murderous weapon might already be lodged in your back.\\n\\n"Since the Battle of Wei Jing, this is already the seventh." The Personal Guard commander's blood-stained boot slams heavily onto the traitor's shoulder. "My lord, be aware—this vermin eats the emperor's salary yet does not hesitate to turn his blade upon his own countrymen. This humble servant begs that his head be hung at the camp gate, to deter others who might harbor the same ambitions."
Behead Him
Such petty schemers who abandon loyalty and righteousness deserve death at anyone's hands
Send to the Magistrate
Let the local officials handle these matters
Others will think twice before acting, remembering the fate of this traitor.
Heavily Guarded
With the forces behind him still unclear, such vermin should be dealt with by our own people. But now that he is no longer in our hands, the future has become harder to control.
Freedom of Movement
The operation failed, but I managed to escape with my life. The next target won't be so fortunate. The next target...
Counterespionage Scheme
Bribe the Hidden Agents
Those blinded by greed will serve anyone
Diplomatic Stance: %+n with the Rebel Lords of Nan Yang
Diplomatic Stance: %+n with the Dissenter Lords of Jin Shen
Khan of Heaven

During the third Northern Campaign against the Chaos Wastes, the dragon banner swept across corrupted grasslands, and thousands of tribesmen broke free of Chaos's chains, hanging the totems of their herds beside the dragon banner in the wars that followed.\\nNow, amid the yurts and felt tents of the southern steppe, the morning bells and evening drums of Zhen Dan echo, and some tribes have resolved to join Zhen Dan against Chaos, honoring Zhen Dan's ruler with the title of Heavenly Khan. Yet these herders, who have never once laid eyes upon the Dragon Emperor Sovereign, do not know who Zhen Dan's true ruler is. The tribal envoy who has come to present his tribute trembles ceaselessly before you—he believes you are their Heavenly Khan.
Accept the tribal title of honor
Even the Jade Dragon was once proclaimed the Dragon Emperor by westerners - the barbarians cannot fathom the depth and breadth of Zhen Dan, so a small misunderstanding is only to be expected
Offer the title of Heavenly Khagan to the Dragon Emperor
Zhen Dan's glory is the Dragon Emperor's glory, and the reverse holds equally true. This is not a matter over which we should contend for supremacy
Zhen Dan has never lacked for praise, but such words never fail to stir the heart.
Glory of the Celestial Empire
Your allies from the north will regard you as their true leader, but one can only imagine the expressions on the faces of the other nobles of Zhen Dan upon hearing your new title...
Loyalty of the Hu Tribesmen
Dragon Emperor's Guard
Marching alongside a member of the Dragon Emperor's Guard, you'll always learn a thing or two.
Hao Tian Sword
A blessed sword that has passed through Cathay for centuries, bearing the weight of home and nation, and regarded as a symbol of the Dragon Emperor's favor.
A Stranger in a Strange Land

Ink-dark clouds crush the light of heaven, and war horses across the camps neigh amid the muddy ferry crossing. Soldiers wrapped in armor wade through the pouring rain, iron plate clashing against the curtain of rain until your ears ache. A sudden cry of alarm abruptly seizes your attention—at the center of a whirlpool's woven net, a woman clad in drenched white silk clutches a piece of driftwood, her dazzling golden hair rising and falling in the water.
Spare no effort to save them
Let the Daoists combine their sorcery, and pick out the soldiers who swim best to go into the water. We cannot stand by and watch them die
It is beyond saving
Entering the water in such a torrential storm is nothing short of suicide. I will not let the men under my command take that risk
Princess Safrey

'Thank you, my lord. Had it not been for your rescue, I fear I would have perished in a foreign land alongside the rest of the delegation. I shall write to my kingdom, but before I return to Ulthuan, allow me to repay my debt of life to you.'
Storyteller
'To know what happens next, listen to my next telling...'
The Storyteller

The faded wine banners atop the blue-brick walls curled in the autumn wind. When the warhorses snorted white breath and halted before the government post house, the station master, trembling as he approached, offered up not a welcoming cup but a piece of news that had set the whole city abuzz\\n\\n『My lord, please believe me!』 The old station master's throat bobbed within his wrinkled neck. 『That storyteller at the teahouse in the West Market... he's not even human!』 His withered fingers waved wildly in the dusk. 『He wears a bronze mask all day long, and his tongue never stops, yet he never seems to draw breath; behind him always follow a hundred or so pale rats—they line up to listen to his tales, and bow whenever he raps his gavel-block!』 Onlookers murmured amongst themselves—some suspected he was one of those monstrosities from beneath the ruins of the Dimensional Stone desert, while others claimed he was a monkey-man from Tian Shan\\n\\nJust as you listen with great interest and are about to press further, the bronze bells at the eaves suddenly clang. Beyond the carved lattice window, a squad of Jade Warriors is escorting a black-robed figure down the long street. The man's bronze mask glows faintly green in the twilight, dozens of small rats scurrying about his feet like a living cloak, and each time his chains rattle, they let out chirps like the wailing of infants\\n\\n『The curse of the Dimensional Stone!』 『He must be a monkey-man spy!』 The whispers of the gathered crowd rustle in the autumn wind. The prison is but a hundred paces away, yet with a single word from you, this strange man's path could be turned toward an entirely different fate
Save this person

Though he wears a cloak and mask, you can still tell he is a man of considerable stature. Even held captive by the Jade Warriors, he remains utterly composed - surely no ordinary man. If he could be brought to serve me, the great enterprise might soon be complete!
Turn a blind eye

You hear the storyteller sing: 'A drifting duckweed, a wanderer with no roots to hold; met by chance upon the water, roaming the world's ends, ask me not why' \\n\\nThough this man is held captive by the Jade Warriors, he remains composed and at ease - surely he has some plan of his own. The road is long; we shall meet again in the world beyond
Your soldiers gave everything to contend against the forces of nature. Though they ultimately achieved their goal, the exhaustion of their bodies will linger with them for a while.
[[col:red]]Exhausted Soldiers[[/col]]

Strange tales of this remarkable storyteller grow ever more fearsome as they pass from mouth to mouth. The common people are both wary and curious - it seems that wherever you go these days, no small stir will follow.
Accompanied by a Peculiar Talent
Ten Proposals for Military Reform

The Ten Proposals for Military Reform was authored by [Sky-Defying Sovereign] Yi Qing, recording a series of frontier army reforms he devised. Yi Qing advocated for the large-scale formation of cavalry units at Chang Yuan, using armored heavy cavalry to break enemy lines in formation, thereby countering the Chaos tribes' hit-and-run tactics of light cavalry harassing infantry formations. The proposal is divided into nine chapters, covering everything from the selection of cavalrymen and armor regulations to banners and battle formations\\n\\nYi Qing's vision had already shown initial success in the Wasteland Campaign: the Northern Expedition Army mobilized three thousand armored cavalry from across the region, forming ranks like a copper wall, moving like thunderbolts—the clatter of horse armor shook the Khan's tent camp even ten li away. The northern light cavalry, accustomed to circling volleys of arrows, were for the first time ground into pulp by heavy cavalry mid-charge\\n\\nThe officials of the Ministry of War sneered in their memorials: 『Such a scheme of chasing the branch while abandoning the root—how can it be held up as a model?』 Some renowned generals dismissed Yi Qing's strategy outright: the armies of Zhen Dan had long grown accustomed to warfare centered on heavy infantry, and the northern troops relied more on Chang Yuan's formidable passes, favoring defense over offense. To now speak of relying heavily on cavalry—was this not asking the Three Armies to tear everything down and start anew? Worse still, some accused Yi Qing of adopting barbarian dress and mounted archery, forgetting his roots and currying favor with the Di tribes, seeking to lay blame upon him
Support Yi Qing

The nature of warfare is ever-changing. We must learn swiftly from frontline experience to remain undefeated in a hundred battles. Though it cannot yet be applied across all of Zhen Dan, it may be tested within a single army, and perhaps prove its worth
Maintain the status quo

'Our Zhen Dan's divine soldiers are unrivaled beneath the heavens, and all within the Four Seas submit before us. How dare this green upstart, appearing from who-knows-where, presume to teach me how to command an army?'
Your army needs time to complete its reforms, and certain vested interests will not sit idly by while you rewrite their rules.
[[col:red]]Resistance to Reform[[/col]]
Every Man's Duty

As dusk hangs low but has not yet fallen, your army wades through the last shallow stream. Hooves churn the gentle glow reflected in the water, startling a flock of cranes among the reeds. Watching those streaks of deep crimson scatter in panic, you suddenly recall the roster of the fallen you reviewed in your tent last autumn—those names struck through with vermilion ink.\\n"Reporting, General—there are followers at the rear of the column."\\nYour adjutant's voice startles the dew from the tip of your riding crop. Following the ranks with your eyes, you see a dozen or so youths emerging from the wheat fields, gripping crude spears with uneasy hands, their coarse hemp jackets dusted with grain. The one in front looks about sixteen or seventeen, like a fresh shoot just pulled from the earth.\\n"This subordinate has already sent men to dissuade them three times." The adjutant's voice carries a hint of rust. "They say... they say they wish to follow my lord, to have their names remembered in history."\\nYour hand clenches the reins in a sudden spasm—these hands have broken the curved sabers of a thousand enemy chieftains, yet cannot bear the spark flying from this boy's eyes. The wind carries the sweet scent of ripening wheat, mingled with the faint smell of blood drifting through the ranks—those veterans who remain forever beneath the walls of Chang Yuan looked just as green before they marched to war.\\n"Let them follow the supply train." Your gesture as you wave them off is like snapping a dry branch. "When we reach the next relay station... distribute the fallen soldiers' old armor to them."\\nThe setting sun sinks toward the distant hills, quenching the fields in molten gold.\\nYou suddenly see the true nature of those "spears"—nothing more than sharpened bamboo poles, fresh sap still oozing from their cut ends.
Take them in as retainers
When the realm rises or falls, every commoner bears responsibility. We must not betray these young men's sincere devotion. If fortune favors them, they may yet have their names written into history
Drive them away with harsh words
'Utterly without discipline! A pack of green boys who don't know their place, wanting to tag along with my army? Send them packing'

The young men sent home will surely tell everyone, indignant, that you have failed and disgraced their wish to serve the nation. But you cannot watch them march to their deaths - after all, the people carry the future of Zhen Dan.
Image Collapse

Your renown spreads throughout Zhen Dan. Now that you have set this precedent for these young men, people from other regions will likewise flock to join your army. You know the fate that awaits most of them, but you also know that in this hour of national crisis, every patriot's sacrifice brings final victory that much closer.
Coming in Droves
An Improper Promotion

You stand upon the jade steps with hands clasped behind your back, surveying the group of newly appointed household commandants. Blood not yet wiped away still traces its path across the armor of these fierce warriors, who stand with straight spines like unsheathed blades. Just as you incline your head to offer praise, an uproar suddenly erupts beyond the camp gate.\\n\\n"My lord, hear us!" The furious Jade Warriors push past the Golden Guard's obstruction and burst into the courtyard, their leader shaking a yellowed sheet of paper until it rattles. "How can such vermin be fit to hold the rank of commandant!" The ink upon the silk paper cuts like a blade, plainly bearing the private seal of the Bureau of Merit Evaluation's director. The young household commandant thus named staggers backward, his jade-inlaid wrist guard striking the blue brick with a jarring, sharp sound.\\n\\nYou fix your gaze upon him, and the youth's face has already turned ashen. Just moments ago at the training grounds, his quick and adaptive battle formation had earned your admiration. The Jade Warriors' knuckles whiten as if to tear through the silk paper, and the murmurs of onlookers have already swelled into a rising clamor. You must make a decision.
Insist on the promotion
I shall deal with his misconduct separately, but such talent should not be allowed to go to waste
Enforce the law impartially
We cannot allow such injustice to stand. Both this Overseer and anyone who accepted his bribes will be thoroughly investigated to the end
You should understand that turning a blind eye to such conduct will surely be noticed by others...
Breeding Corruption
The noble shall be rewarded, and the vile shall find no refuge.
Strict Military Discipline
The character has a chance of being wounded
Your decision is bold, but not everyone shares your point of view.
An Uneasy Retinue
A Hu tribal army has gathered at Chang Yuan, ready to pledge their loyalty to you
[Right Worthy Prince] Wu Daruoti
Fulfill your duty
Chang Yuan shelters every citizen of Zhen Dan behind it. We too must fulfill our duty
Give generously
With your generous contribution, Chang Yuan's armaments will grow abundant, and more soldiers will be sent to reinforce it
Above Chang Yuan

Zhen Dan has weathered countless springs and autumns under the shelter of Chang Yuan. Since the Dragon Emperor's decree, the noble houses of the Nine Sons and Ten Surnames have each season dispatched their fief's annual tribute to the frontier pass—brocade wrapped in patterned weaves, bearing the weight of jade beads, ultimately transformed into blades in the hands of the frontier army, and beacon smoke atop the watchtowers.\\n\\nThe crossbows of Long Men Pass await the fine arrows of Kun Lan; the granaries of Ao Men Pass await the rice of Nong Chang. Before the sundial completes its turn, the convoys of the noble houses shall set out for Chang Yuan in succession, for the strokes of the court historian's brush are carved into the bricks of Chang Yuan, enduring longer than any ancestral tablet of nanmu wood in any shrine.
Spare no effort to help
With this vast support, the Celestial Dynasty's most elite forces can be deployed to the front lines
A conscripted peasant army will reinforce Chang Yuan.
A Jade Valor Legion will reinforce Chang Yuan.
A Dragon Guard Celestial Army will reinforce Chang Yuan.
Line your own pockets
Zhen Dan is vast and rich in resources, with so many powers already supporting Chang Yuan - surely my contribution alone won't matter much either way...
You chose to protect yourself in the face of the greater cause of hearth and home. In the short term, this may have been the best choice for you, but the rest of Zhen Dan will not see it that way.
[[col:red]]Deeply Controversial[[/col]]
Battle of Wei Jing

Ash and embers scatter, lighting up the night—the rebellion of the Prince of Nan Yang has torn open the curtain of chaos upon the Celestial Court. He was once among Zhen Dan's greatest generals, sweeping away rebellious warlords for the Celestial Court. Yet now his spearhead points at the capital itself. Former comrades have turned against one another, brothers-in-arms now clash blade to blade. Ye Jiang Zhou is, in the eyes of the frontier army, a typical southerner—these scholars who grew up beside the canals have enjoyed all the wealth that trade brought them, grown accustomed to the good life of boating and moon-watching, able to argue philosophy with eloquence, yet possessing no real skill—though in truth, this too was merely the imaginings of others. The Celestial Dynasty's territory is simply too vast; most people of Zhen Dan spend their entire lives circling within the small plot of land where they were born, only able to savor a taste of the wider world through the tales told by storytellers. Since the conscription began at Wai Li Village, Ye Jiang Zhou traveled in a mere half-month to Fu Hong, a place he could only dream of in his previous nineteen years. Like his fellow villagers, Ye Jiang Zhou had assumed he would pick tea leaves his whole life. Fu Hong's martial tradition is renowned throughout the Nine Provinces, but in the old days, the Militia Legions and Beacon-Keepers never let common folk go to war. Some days ago, a Beacon-Keeper unit passed through Wai Li to drink tea before heading south beyond the dense forest, and Ye Jiang Zhou, curious how these masked warriors ate, secretly brought his little sister along to find out—only to discover that once they removed their helmets, they looked no different from ordinary people. Still, this did nothing to diminish Ye Jiang Zhou's admiration for these soldiers; he knew these silent warriors had always guarded the Celestial Dynasty on battlefields he had never witnessed. Times have grown far harder than before, but the Celestial Court's decree brooks no refusal from the pacification commissioners, and Peasant Levies from hundreds of villages along the Grand Canal were all summoned to the provincial capital, then sent north as one. Everything happened too suddenly, leaving this naive young man dizzy with confusion. On the road north, Ye Jiang Zhou still thought of Fu Hong—he only regretted not agreeing to let his little sister come with him to the provincial capital. He had finally tasted the plum blossom cakes his sister always talked about, their fragrance making even him crave more; at the very least, he should ask someone to bring a bag home for her. It was not until reaching The Pearl that Ye Jiang Zhou's thoughts were pulled back to reality by sheer astonishment. Though every province had already begun conscription, this magnificent city remained bustling with activity. The Pearl is Zhen Dan's second-largest metropolis, but most people of Zhen Dan have no concept of the gap between rumor and reality until they actually visit. Jiang Zhou was so stunned his mouth hung open, and the roar of the crowd nearly deafened him. He had heard the village storyteller speak of The Pearl and thought it all mythical exaggeration, but now, truly seeing those towers piercing the clouds, he suddenly recalled the village storyteller's saying, 'the higher one climbs, the colder it grows'—he knew the phrase's original meaning, yet still could not suppress a shiver. Even from The Pearl, one could glimpse the Celestial Court at Wei Jing to the northeast—did those dragons dwelling among the clouds, in that cold and lofty sky, also shiver from the chill?\\nIt was also at The Pearl that the Peasant Levies' journey came to a stop. The night before, Ye Jiang Zhou had heard from his fellow villagers that they might soon follow the pacification commissioner into the capital, and he had lain awake all night in excitement. But dawn came, and he never even saw the accompanying Militia Legions—instead, orders came directly reassigning them to Chang Yuan. Only then did he learn from the frontier army officer leading them that the capital was already packed with high officials and nobles, and the generals and dignitaries of all fifteen provinces within the passes had already gathered there by imperial decree, awaiting the command of that noble who issued the order—like so many pieces on a game board. And they, mere Peasant Levies, clearly had no place there. Though told they would fight at Chang Yuan, reality left Ye Jiang Zhou in a half-dreaming daze—the endless walls stretching beyond sight already left him disoriented, and the frontier soldiers seemed unwilling to let these tea farmers, untrained in arms, actually enter battle. Ye Jiang Zhou drilled daily beneath the walls of Chang Yuan's inner city, and the villages along the wall bustled with life, just like his hometown—only missing his noisy little sister. Though the villagers looked after her, he could not help but worry; he had never been apart from her for so long. Fu Hong's pacification commissioner had only shouted a few words to them, but Jiang Zhou trusted that portly middle-aged man—had he asked at the time, perhaps he might have let his sister come north to see the world too.\\nThree weeks have passed since he was first reassigned to Chang Yuan, and the days beneath the wall remain unchanged from when he arrived, except that messengers rushing in and out of the city walls grow ever more frequent. Ye Jiang Zhou heard that foreign devils from across the sea now ravage the east, and the harm wrought by these things—neither man nor ghost—is more terrifying than the calamity brought by the Dark Elves a decade past. Countless villages have been burned to ash, tens of thousands of Zhen Dan soldiers have died at Xuan Yuan, and the fleeing refugees have left The Pearl gasping under the crowd's weight. He thinks he now understands why Fu Hong's pacification commissioner went to such lengths to conscript humble folk like himself—perhaps it was right, after all, not to bring his little sister. Jiang Zhou had always dreamed of being a wandering knight; he grew up on stories of the [Giant Hero], and hoped one day to live as freely and righteously as in those tales, protecting home and country. But hearing news of fellow villagers dying at Xuan Yuan, he felt a flicker of relief—his little sister still waited for him at home, and Chang Yuan was a safe place. This magnificent line of defense stretching across the Celestial Dynasty's north remains, in the hearts of all Zhen Dan's people, an unshakable symbol. Once the eastern war ends, perhaps he can return home—perhaps even use his merit from guarding the frontier to take his sister on a proper journey to see the world.\\n\\nThe majestic Palace Guard stands outside your tent, and Zhen Dan awaits your command. You have already rescinded the decree calling for reinforcements from the provinces of He Dong to the Three Passes, and even redirected additional reinforcements from the assembled armies, but the destruction wrought by the Norscans has still exceeded your advisors' earlier estimates. Should Chaos's armies truly follow close behind, even greater sacrifice will be unavoidable. Chang Yuan still stands in the north, and so long as the Three Passes remain unfallen, all remains within your control—but the forces of destruction brook no testing, and Zhen Dan's fate allows for no trial and error. If the Chang Yuan line of defense truly proves unable to hold, where then shall we turn?

Reclaiming the Dong Feng Fortress was only the beginning of it all.\\n\\nYet another contemptible Pink Horror was torn apart beneath the fierce crossbows of Zhen Dan, but for these creatures from beyond, death is merely a stepping stone to new life. The felt tents lay silent as tombs, and herders with their eyes gouged out huddled in the shadows. The Celestial Dynasty's cavalry, after long years, once more crossed the Twelve Linked Mountains of the desert, but the corruption of Chaos had utterly erased the once lush pastures of old.\\n\\n"The surrender proceeds as expected, my lord Raging Gale," said Fang Wen Zi, arms full of scrolls, as he approached Miao Ying. "Most have chosen to accept our rule, but the corruption of the desert runs too deep — in every tribe there are some who remain... stubbornly defiant." He drew forth a scroll from the pile and spread it across Miao Ying's table — a map of the southern desert marked with intricate lines. "But I've already dealt with those uprisings. The fleeing rebels, without exception, retreated toward the mountains to the north — very near the edge of the Dragon Emperor's past campaigns."\\n\\n"Where did this come from? Did we have detailed maps of these regions before?" Miao Ying's brow rose slightly. "I drew it myself last night, my lord. That is not the point, however. The locals regard those mountains as the edge of the world, but I believe even by their own understanding of geography, they know the continent's true boundary lies far beyond. This is some manner of religious devotion, my lord — the Astronomical Bureau confirms the magical winds in that mountain range are unnaturally active. The reports from our scouts remain unclear — their minds were badly shaken. They say they could hear whispers there, a certain name... something is surely amiss."\\n\\n"This is the Chaos Wastes, Fang Wen Zi. Nothing that happens here should surprise us." "Yes, my lord, but if we are to bring this region fully under control, we must unravel this mystery. My lord, the place the herders call the edge of the mountains — the answer to our northern campaign lies there."
Break Through the Encirclement!
[[col:white]]Wei Bei Provinces[[/col]] · The Great Sacrifice

Miao Ying began to regret not having personally investigated Dong Feng Fortress thoroughly.\\n\\nNow her army stood at the very center of the ritual array.\\n\\nThe great victory won upon the wastes brought joy to the Raging Gale, yet her sharp mind did not slacken because of it. The dragons had contended with Chaos for a thousand years; she had never underestimated this unfathomable foe. But could that hard-won triumph have been merely a thread within a greater snare? None had foreseen it. The power of Chaos had sunk deep into the ley lines — this sickening desolation was proof enough.\\n\\n"I should have known!" To offer life as sacrifice was ever the way of Chaos, even when the altar was an entire battlefield, an entire wasteland.\\n\\n"I believe even the Moon Empress would not blame herself in such circumstances, my lord Raging Gale." Fang Wen Zi's voice, amid the clashing ranks, sounded like a whisper carried from ten thousand miles away, yet Miao Ying had grown used to hearing it as a great bell's toll — this mortal possessed an understanding of the world more profound than most, perhaps even more than her own, and he served as the measure that kept the Raging Gale's actions true.\\n\\n"A ritual of this scale is unheard of. Even with a rift to the Realm of Chaos so near, even with so many lives offered as sacrifice, the army it could summon would still fall far short of what would be needed." Fang Wen Zi struggled to keep his footing amid the shrieking of sorcery; his voice remained steady, though sweat streaked down his cheeks. Miao Ying could see that the current situation had already exceeded even the imagination of the [Moon Immortal].\\n\\n"We must fall back to Xue Feng — I mean, Dong Feng Fortress. Yi Qing's cavalry should be able to arrive in time, but the enemy's numbers... no, we cannot muster reinforcements of sufficient scale right now. But I might still work with the other Astronomical Officers to use the magical wind node at Dong Feng Fortress to block—"\\n\\n"Dong Feng Fortress has already fallen! Fang Wen Zi, has your gift for the Winds of Magic truly failed to sense that pitiful tremor? The node at Dong Feng Fortress was itself part of the ritual array — we are already isolated. We fight, or we die!" Fang Wen Zi's words kindled a nameless fury within Miao Ying. She had believed the [Moon Immortal] could cover the blind spots of the Dragon Eyes, but he had failed her expectations... no, no — in the end, it was she who had chosen to press forward. She was merely casting the blame for her own misstep onto this poor mortal. Tens of thousands of frontier soldiers' lives still rested in her hands; now was no time to let herself be blinded by rage.\\n\\n"Forget what I said, Fang Wen Zi. We break through to the south — Ao Men Pass is but a stone's throw from here. I will not sit idle while the soldiers of Zhen Dan are buried in this place!" A flicker of bewilderment crossed Fang Wen Zi's eyes — was he calculating the odds of breaking through, or startled by the Raging Gale's sudden shift in temper? Miao Ying no longer cared. He was but one among the thousands of mortals at her back, and she had sworn to bring every one of them home.

[[col:white]]I am the beloved daughter of the Dragon Emperor.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:white]]I am the Governor-Marshal of the Wei Bei provinces.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:white]]I am the Lord of the Great Bastion.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:white]]I will never yield![[/col]]\\n\\nThe slaughter raged on through the entire day. Miao Ying's strength was boundless, yet as the floodwaters surged, her killing intent proved no vessel to carry them all to safety. Her storm churned among the clouds, her wrath boiled within the ranks, but her claws could not hold back the shifting sands, nor recall the lives scattering like dust. The defenses on every side teetered on the brink of collapse. The Dragon Eyes met the vacant gaze of the dead — the mortals she had sworn to bring home now lay in rivers of blood. The Raging Gale howled at the heavens, her claws rending the Chaos Warriors that assailed her from every direction, her teeth snapping the slender neck of a bird-shaped daemon — why was this savage divine power so utterly useless! The Dragon Emperor's honor meant nothing here; the echo of shattered lives rang loud and clear.\\n\\n"My lord Raging Gale... bring them home." Miao Ying heard that bell-like voice once more.\\n\\nFang Wen Zi struggled to rise behind her, his mortal frame already so small before the undying dragon body — now, this gaunt, blood-streaked man resembled the last kindling before a storm's end.\\n\\n"I did all I could, Fang Wen Zi. I truly did all I could, I..." His broken fingers reached to touch the tip of the Raging Gale's claw, and a sudden, piercing cold cut her words short.\\n\\n"My lord Raging Gale, you have already done enough." His voice was weary, aged, nearly a whisper. Fang Wen Zi's mastery over the Winds of Magic had touched the very pinnacle a mortal could reach, but he was, in the end, only a mortal — and sustaining this desperate battle had drained the last of his life.\\n\\n"Behind the dragons, mortals feel this helplessness of yours in every passing moment, and yet we have come this far. You were born as miracles, and so cannot imagine what would seem a miracle even to yourselves; mortals are born small, yet having witnessed miracles walk among them throughout their lives, we come to conceive the thought of creating miracles of our own." Miao Ying watched dust scatter from his shoulders — this soul on the edge of death now blazed as bright as a shooting star.\\n\\n"Fang Wen Zi, what are you doing."\\n\\n"The Dragon Emperor rescued the people of this land from darkness. He walked among mortal flesh, created Zhen Dan, and wrote our history."\\n\\n"Stop this at once — that is my order."\\n\\n"Dragon... do not be afraid."\\n\\n"Stop, now!"\\n\\n"You need not... *cough*... walk alone into the night."\\n\\n"Fang Wen Zi, don't!"\\n\\n"Beside you... walks a mortal soul."\\n\\nDawn broke.\\n\\nA warm wind carried the dust back home.\\n\\nAnd upon the wasteland, the Skybridge rose from nothing.

[[col:white]]Wei Bei Provinces[[/col]] · Unforeseen

As if born anew.\\n\\nFang Wen Zi woke atop the mountain, his eyes stinging from the sunlight, the gravel biting into his back — yet he should have been crushed to dust beneath the weight of the magic wind he had wielded.\\n\\n"This is..."\\n\\n"You're awake, Fang Wen Zi." Miao Ying sat beside him, as calm and stern as ever — were it not for the mottled bloodstains upon her armor, Fang Wen Zi might have doubted the whole desperate battle had been but a dream. "Well done. I have witnessed the miracle you wrought."\\n\\nFang Wen Zi nearly felt shame — he had truly been prepared to give his life, and yet, once again, the outcome had exceeded expectation. "I spoke out of turn, my lord Raging Gale. Please, do not mock me — what has truly happened here?"\\n\\n"I am not mocking you, Fang Wen Zi. Opening the Skybridge from nothing — Father might think little of such a feat, but us? As far as I know, not one among my imperial kin could achieve such a thing." Fang Wen Zi tried to read some trace of emotion from the dragon-kin's face, but that jade visage remained as ever — unchanging, ageless, expressionless.\\n\\n"Not even you?"\\n\\n"Not even I, Fang Wen Zi." Miao Ying shook her head slowly, her face unreadable as ever.\\n\\n"I have always regarded humans as that same fragile race from a thousand years ago — helpless and faltering without us, having made no progress in all these years save in the arts of scheming and rivalry." She rose to her feet, turning her back to the still-immobile mortal, her silhouette blotting out the sun. Fang Wen Zi closed his eyes; he could sense those dragon eyes gazing straight into the sunrise, and though he knew that face always held nothing at all, he could not help but wonder now at the expression the Raging Gale wore.\\n\\n"You have changed how I see things, Fang Wen Zi — not just you, but all those who fought bravely at our side. How could we possibly have fought our way out otherwise? If you mortals keep creating miracles like this, I may need to find some name other than 'mortal' for your kind." Miao Ying's voice carried neither joy nor sorrow, like some distant, ethereal oracle, and surely that face bore the same detachment — a veil, a miracle. "Now, get up, Fang Wen Zi. I said I would bring you all home — you're the only one left."\\n\\nHe opened his eyes.\\n\\nHe had guessed wrong.\\n\\nUpon that jade visage was etched an unforgettable smile.

How much time remains before the prophecy of the Vast Heavens comes to pass? How much longer can we wait? Father told me everything he and Mother had glimpsed, and then entrusted the execution of the great scheme to me, for he believed I could still make the right choice even knowing the despair of that outcome. Ball after ball of fire burst through the thick dust thrown up by the violent impacts. The Terror Cannons' volleys roared like thunder, tearing down the overburdened walls of Long Men Pass, leaving spiraling smoke in the air like ink dropped into a stream. Amid the ruined walls, blazing fire still danced, the deep scars left by bombardment as astonishing as some vast wound carved into Zhen Dan's very flesh. Ye Jiang Zhou hurried through the scorching heat, the nightmarish scene leaving him dazed. He still remembered vividly the day the decree was proclaimed, the dazzling dragon banners of the Imperial Guard, the armies of the fifteen provinces gathered in full — nearly a million soldiers filling every inch of land as far as the eye could see. That was the first time he truly understood Zhen Dan's might; never had he felt so filled with strength. The Celestial Court's decree had rung out like thunder: Zhen Dan would defend Chang Yuan at any cost, and no one — friend or foe — would be allowed to cross that line.\\nAt the front were the Dragon Guards, then the Jade Braves — corpses piled into small hills beneath the walls, soldier after soldier throwing themselves forward to no avail. The boundary of the mortal world had been torn asunder, and the power of Chaos seemed without end. The defenders had fallen back to the last line, fewer than ten thousand survivors remaining. Ye Jiang Zhou could hear the generals arguing, could see their expressions slowly hardening: both Kui Men and Ao Men passes had fallen in succession, Long Men now stood nearly isolated, and it seemed only annihilation awaited them — first themselves, then all of Zhen Dan. Tears welled up in his eyes; Ye Jiang Zhou thought of his little sister, of his homeland — if everything was destined to be destroyed, what meaning could sacrifice possibly hold?\\n\\nYe Jiang Zhou stood alongside the frontier army's soldiers; they would cover the retreat of the last elite troops from the Three Passes back to Wei Jing. As long as even a shred of strength remained, as long as they had not given up, Zhen Dan's fate was not yet sealed. Ye Jiang Zhou gazed out at the vast enemy host arraying itself for the final assault — this, then, was to be his end.\\n'Soldiers, fight beside me! History will forever remember this day, and Zhen Dan will forever remember our names!' Yes — at the very least, he would die like a hero. The last of the frontier army roared and charged at the horde of demons, like waves striving to slay the sea itself.\\nThe bombardment of the Terror Cannons continued unabated, as though the entire world wailed as one. Waves of all-consuming fire toppled buildings, and the streets boiled with surging flame. Ye Jiang Zhou lay among the corpses; he had never imagined he could cut down those seemingly unshakeable minions of Chaos — how many had he killed? He could no longer recall. Long Men Pass was swallowed by blazing fire, sharp pain seeping into every part of his body, blood and heat rising together into vapor.\\nThen darkness finally fell, and Ye Jiang Zhou felt nothing more.
