Yet another branch of the rebellion has met its end, as Ye Sheng—who had drowned himself in pleasure through a string of defeats—finally reached his final reckoning\\nFeng Yao, whom the traitorous minister had relied upon as his right hand, led his enraged troops storming into the inner palace. Ye Sheng and his faction of Hong Wu Overseers made their last stand in the great hall. Seeing that the assault could not break through, Feng Yao ordered his men to set the place ablaze. The defenders, their bodies wreathed in flame, fled in panic from the fire only to be pinned by crossbowmen's bolts against the outer terrace. The blaze burned throughout the entire night; the wailing gradually died away, yet the flames climbed ever higher, consuming charred flesh and blood alongside the very jewels, wine, and meat they had once feasted upon without restraint as kindling. The common folk whispered uneasily of the eerie visions rising within the flames, but the soldiers who took part in the coup remained unmoved—betrayal and retribution had long become routine to them. Their eyes gleamed in the firelight as they eagerly fought over the mountains of grain piled in the storehouses, desperate to fill their own starved and suffering bellies\\nAll verdicts and judgments can wait until dawn

The world is crumbling. The forces of Destruction strike from every direction, and the Old World clings to survival beneath the threat of calamity. Evil spirits from all corners of the earth devour the lands of the Celestial Empire piece by piece. The Celestial Court now lies within your grasp—from there you shall command the capital region, command Zhen Dan, and command every living creature that dwells within it. Never since the Dragon Emperor's retreat into seclusion has Zhen Dan been so powerful, yet never has it faced a crisis such as this. We need greater strength still—the entire cosmos shall bend to your will. Show us the way forward

Your edicts have spread across all the land, and generals and commanders from all quarters have followed the Celestial Court's strategy, mustering their forces for war\\nThe beacon fires already burn, and the hearts of the myriad people turn as one. The Celestial Empire's million-strong army stands ready to give its life in service\\nIn this hour of survival, only flesh and blood can defend our mountains and rivers, our sacred realm\\nGlory to Zhen Dan! All for the Dragon Emperor!

The fighting in the north grows ever fiercer. The frontier army is now conscripting skilled craftsmen from across the nation to reinforce the city walls and strengthen the fortifications, ensuring the border passes remain impregnable. This is a matter of national importance, and every province has already made its stance known—the repairs to Chang Yuan will soon commence. Perhaps we should not remain uninvolved

Gelt led a company of Gold Wizards, arriving at Chang Yuan alongside a relief convoy from the Wei Xi Provinces. Though the frontier army initially refused to let their magic touch Chang Yuan, upon seeing Bin Long's handwritten imperial decree, the ritual of the Wind of Metal was at last allowed to proceed—now a magnificent golden barrier flows along the outer walls of Chang Yuan, its power merging into the ceaseless torrent of aethyric winds coursing through this immortal fortress

The Shang Yang Martial Trial is an event long anticipated across all of Zhen Dan, a gathering fated for heroes and champions of every domain. With each trial, the mighty from all corners of Zhen Dan—and even the Old World—gather like converging stars upon Shang Yang. Banners snap in the fierce wind, the faint glow of runes intertwining with the cold gleam of blades, as heaven and earth hold their breath awaiting the birth of a champion.\\n\\nAs is custom, the Bin Tie Court has sent invitations to the provinces. Should we send representatives to attend this rare and grand event? This may well be a rare opportunity.

The sand of the arena burns hot beneath the sun, the noisy crowd's murmurs mingling with camel bells and low Arabian chants. Your champion steps into the arena, where an Arabian scimitar-wielder wrapped in an indigo turban already awaits, running his fingers over the cold gleam of the blade at his waist, sand crunching softly beneath his boots. "The rules didn't say I couldn't kill, did they?" he growls under his breath, his form suddenly shifting as twin scimitars carve two arcs of cold light through the sunlight, charging forward on his own initiative—his footwork elusive, his blades aimed squarely at vital points, each strike meant to kill.

The arena feels solemn today, banners bearing the characters for "Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth" hanging on all four sides. A monk of Fu Hong, clad in brown robes, sits cross-legged upon the scorching sand, palms pressed together, his breath as steady as a mountain—this clamorous arena feels no different to him than the meditation chamber he calls home. The horn signaling the start of the match blares deafeningly, and only then does the Five Elements monk slowly rise, his toes tapping lightly against the ground, which faintly glows in response. "Forgive my rudeness, benefactor," he says—and with those words, his form shifts suddenly, his palms forming shapes now rigid as an ancient pine, now fluid as flowing water, the winds of elemental energy surging across his palms as elemental power begins to boil.

The arena's fencing has been reinforced threefold, the crowd's cheers tinged with unease. A strongman from the Path of Long Tusks strides forward—this dark-skinned giant stands even taller than an ordinary Ogre, his bare torso covered in gruesome scars, the stone hammer at his side stained with the blood of some unfortunate previous contestant. "ROAAAR—!" His bellow rings through everyone's ears like rolling thunder, and the strongman charges at his diminutive opponent, swinging his weapon with sheer brute force—these wide, sweeping strikes seem full of openings, yet they keep any foe from drawing near, the wind kicked up by each blow as bone-chilling as a mountain gale, the reverberations of each impact shaking the entire arena—this is raw power enough to crush any foe.

Banners snap in the wind, yet cannot drown out the whispers rippling through the stands—every eye is fixed on the shadows in the northwest corner, where last year's champion leans against the wall, the undefeated Martial Fanatic, the last one left to defend his title—Pei Yue. A figure in dark battle garb emerges from the shadows, the champion's bare arms covered in scars, wounds left by defeated challengers who gave everything they had, now serving as marks of his legend. You had heard that the retainers of Bin Long care little for the customs of the Central Plains, but you never imagined the Martial Fanatic would be quite this arrogant. As the horn blares deafeningly, Pei Yue begins to stride forward slowly, rubbing his arm, cracking his neck, utterly ignoring the champion charging straight at him. "Just another stepping stone," he says—before you can even make out his words, your champion is sent flying through the air, slamming heavily into the sand. As the dust settles, Pei Yue walks out from the cloud of sand, finally turning his gaze upon his struggling opponent as he rises. "You'd best last longer than those so-called grandmasters."

Upon the arena of the Shang Yang Martial Trial, gilded banners snap in the fierce wind. Your champion steps onto the great stage of the semi-final trial, while you stand in the shadows of the viewing platform, keenly aware of the gazes of strongmen from every domain of Zhen Dan upon you—scrutiny mixed with curiosity about the unknown. Regret arrives at last: in the fierce struggle against a fated rival, though your champion poured a lifetime of martial skill into every strike, each blow etched with loyalty and valor, in the end he fell just short, defeated in bitter regret. The referee's declaration cuts through the clamor, cheers surging like the tide across the arena, the fierce wind sweeping past plain cloth, bringing a brief silence—as if heaven and earth themselves mourned for the defeated. Your champion bows, his body wracked with wounds, for victory and defeat are but a footnote beneath the wheels of history; the martial prowess of your court's warrior has been etched into the sight of all Zhen Dan's domains, and that alone is enough.

As the final horn of the championship match pierces the fierce wind, cheers sweep across the arena like thunder. You stand atop the highest platform of the viewing stand, receiving the admiration and congratulations of all Zhen Dan's domains—your champion, having fought through countless rivals, has finally overcome the Martial Fanatic Pei Yue in the ultimate showdown, claiming for you the crown of this grand martial event that has shaken all of Zhen Dan. The people of your domain are already roaring with joy, drums and cheers sweeping through the streets like waves, offering their most ardent praise to this glory; strongmen from every land have sent envoys bearing gifts—tributes that carry not only recognition of the champion's glory, but also awe for your own authority as their lord.

My lord, all Eight Great Daoist Sects under Heaven have answered the call! The masters of every school, leading their disciples, race through the night toward the Nong Chang Basin. They shall march straight for the Mausoleum of Poet Yan Mo, vowing to sever the very source of the Jade Blood curse!

My lord, the Jade Blood Daoist Temple of Weng Chang has already answered our call first. Three hundred Daoists now cross the river, sailing downstream—they will attempt to join with the [Jade Bone Immortal] at Nong Chang, to bring an end to the Curse of Jade Blood once and for all.

The Daoists had prepared for every eventuality, having come precisely to sever this curse for good.\\nThe most renowned grandmasters under Heaven stood arrayed in formation, the combined arts of a hundred sects an unstoppable force. They sealed the Blood Lord upon the mausoleum altar, beheaded the blood-descendants of the Five Clans out in the open, and the summoning ritual of the Jade Corpse could no longer be sustained—victory seemed within reach.\\nBut it now seems they had gravely underestimated the malice concealed within the ley lines themselves.\\nNong Chang is a great maw that swallows life and death alike, blurring the boundary between the two, fusing all things within it into one—and it hungers still.\\nIt hungers for new sacrifice.\\nBlood ran down along the pierced wounds of the Daoists, and from that moment, all was beyond recall.\\nThe bones wailed forth their mournful incantations, the corpses of the blood-descendants twisted and warped, and the Blood Lord's body sank into shadow.\\nThen came the resentment and hunger accumulated over ten thousand years, arriving to devour the final offering.\\nThe grand formation of penetrating truth shook heaven and earth asunder, the mausoleum altar entirely overturned, crushing down upon this cursed land. The sword-qi of the lovestruck Daoist companions leveled five hills, Guang Cheng reversed the sorcery of the undead, sending the heroic spirits of the dragon altar surging into the heart of the battle. The Five Elements arts of the Daoists wrought violent upheaval upon the very heavens—at that moment, the people of the southern lands could still see, a hundred miles distant, the roaring clouds and crashing thunder. But by then it was no longer about glory, nor about righteous cause—only life-or-death struggle could still offer a sliver of hope.\\nThey had once driven the Jade Blood Clan to the very brink of annihilation, yet in the end found no burial ground of their own.\\nThe corpses scattered across the ground rose all at once, and the Sovereign of the Void pressed together the two halves of his severed face with a shattered palm, blood flowing backward, returning into his flesh.\\nNow, at last, he had attained the Dao.

Across the realm now, beacon-fires rise on every side, and the age itself totters toward ruin. Though the capital nominally commands the Nine Provinces, it holds no true power to enforce its will—warlords rise on every hand, contending for supremacy. And so the Celestial Court has issued its edict, dispatching envoys to all corners, ostensibly to assist local governance in reforming administration and securing the borders—but in truth, to spread eyes and ears, and keep watch over the various lords. Yet these officials are skilled in governance, in pacifying and administering the people, each following proper method—in these difficult times, they can indeed help us build strength. Whether to accept or refuse, the decision is yours, my lord.

Now beacon-fires burn across all of Zhen Dan, and the realm is thrown into turmoil—the common people, displaced from their homes, struggle to survive amid hunger, cold, and war. Yet your traveling court, through clear-sighted governance and firm city defenses, has carved out a haven of peace in this troubled land. Word has spread by mouth among the fleeing commoners of the four directions, and they arrive one after another—but only you know that this city has only just found its footing, its supplies already stretched thin. How could it possibly take in refugees on such a scale?\\n\\nOutside the city walls, the poor souls ravaged by war have already gathered in great numbers, their pleas to be let inside rising ceaselessly. It is time to make a decision.

Your younger brother, Zhao Ming, has sent you an urgent letter—not through the official channels of the Wei Xi Provinces, but as a private matter between siblings. He claims that among all his brothers and sisters, you are the one he trusts most. The situation in Shang Yang is now somewhat... difficult—the treacherous rebel Jin Shen has dragged nearly every rat-kin in Zhen Dan into his war against him. He truly needs a bit of help now, and he would prefer, very much prefer, that this aid remain private—he doesn't want to still look like the little brother forever trailing behind his elder siblings. And once the troubles in the west are resolved, he will surely repay your kindness today twofold.

'That scum Ye Sheng is finally dead—you would never believe how many brilliant schemes I came up with during this war, I even built a tank in imitation of one! Though it broke down during the very first assault, when it exploded it actually collapsed an entire section of the wall! Ha Ha Ha, you simply wouldn't believe how much I've grown through this war! Yes, truly, so much! It's a pity so many died, but perhaps there was no helping it—after all, that's war! Perhaps in the future I'll think of some new methods, perhaps...\\n\\nAnyway, the rebellion has now been ended. Though I'm not swamped with affairs of state the way you are, I can finally act with a freer hand. Speaking of being swamped—surely you haven't forgotten, amid all your busyness, the great favor I owed you before! Though the letter was private, I've had the ambassador personally deliver the treasures to you—as a token symbolizing the friendship between our provinces, hahaha! There are quite a few fine things inside, you really must take a look—this is what's called repaying twofold, plus a little something extra!\\n\\nHope all goes well for you!\\n————[[col:red]]Your unworthy brother, Zhao Ming[[/col]][[img:wwd_seal]][[/img]]'

The envoy from Nan Yang knelt, trembling, beneath the cloud steps of the Raging Gale's court.\\nSince the fall of the Fallen Hearts, the scattered rebels have wandered in exile, and under the looming threat of Tzeentch, these mortals have become utterly insignificant—their final worth lying only in serving as a warning to other ambitious warlords harboring treacherous designs. The envoy had clearly dressed himself in whatever finery he could scrape together to observe proper etiquette, yet these tattered robes still looked utterly out of place among the temples of the dragons. Though the rebel forces had once struck fear into the northern provinces, their fighting spirit had already shattered—the Prince of Nan Yang's unbroken legend came to an abrupt end at Wei Jing, followed by defeat after defeat. Toppling a high wall is difficult, but once it begins to lean, the slightest disturbance will bring it crashing down.\\n\\nThe Imperial Guard shoved the envoy into the great hall; he collapsed to his knees in a disgraceful heap, not daring to raise his head, feeling only the bitter chill against his neck—that piercing cold pain with a clear purpose: to her own people, the Raging Gale was without doubt a steadfast and reliable leader, but to her enemies, everything was far simpler—she was the very embodiment of nightmare. 'Do you know, I've always thought you traitors were nothing but cowardly vermin—but you, you've made me reconsider somewhat. A rebel who slaughtered his own brothers-in-arms, yet dares to set foot in my court! State your worth at once, or go to the Meridian Gate to meet your death.'\\n\\nThe envoy kowtowed repeatedly, raising his offering high above his head. 'We, in our folly and treachery, rashly raised arms in rebellion—our crime of insurrection deserves ten thousand deaths and cannot be atoned. We humbly beg the Grand Marshal to momentarily set aside her heavenly wrath, and deign to lower her honored gaze upon the contents of this box, before rendering final judgment.' The Imperial Guard took the ornate, luxurious box from him, and Miao Ying sensed within it a stale, musty scent—and a faint warmth.\\n\\nHow disgusting... yet Miao Ying still gestured for the guard to present the nauseating box.\\n\\nInside lay the head of Han Cheng.\\n\\nThe traitors must have spent considerable time preparing it—this was the first time she had seen the Prince of Nan Yang's face untainted by blood and dust.\\n\\nWhat an unpleasant feeling.\\n\\n'We humbly submit: the traitor Han Cheng harbored treacherous designs, secretly conspired with foreign enemies, and colluded covertly with Tzeentch. Over the long years, his crimes accumulated beyond measure, and the common people suffered under his tyranny for far too long—cries of grief echoed through every street, and grievances spread far and wide! When this rebel first stirred his insurrection, he held our families hostage to force our compliance with his rebellion; had we wished to preserve our loyalty, our clans would have first faced annihilation. Constrained by the safety of our households, we were compelled to feign allegiance to the rebel faction, swallowing our shame and bitterness, yet never for a single moment forgetting the grace of the Celestial Court! To bend beneath a rebel's court was as though treading through fire and boiling water, our pent-up fury building until it could no longer be contained! Han Cheng's adopted son, Han Qing, though raised within the rebel's household, never lost his conscience—now that the traitor Han's power wanes and his treacherous schemes lie exposed, Han Qing seized the moment to act on righteousness, slaying the arch-villain with his own hands! This was no mere feat of mortal strength, but truly a manifestation of Heaven's judgment, and also owed to the Grand Marshal's own awesome virtue! We now humbly present the rebel's head before these steps, to make plain our true intentions. We humbly beg the Grand Marshal to look upon our sincerity, forgive our past transgressions, and grant us a path to redemption.'\\n\\nWhat an irritating voice.

The curse of Nong Chang is dissipating\\nAnd so too is the soul of the [Jade Bone Immortal]\\nJin Xiao's neck had long since stiffened; though he could not see himself, the decaying scent his body gave off already betrayed the corruption of the ghastly flesh beneath his jade-like visage. The power of Hao Tian is healing this wounded land, but his own existence is no longer shielded by its peace and harmony. Nong Chang has suffered greatly under the Curse of Jade Blood, but this land is vast enough, and history will grant it ample time—the old wounds will eventually be mended. But what of himself? Jade Blood granted this mortal shell an uncanny power, and then the Jade Dragon's decree concealed its hideous foundation—when the curse is lifted, all abominations bound to its power will crumble along with it.\\n\\nJin Xiao raised his hand, watching jade dust drift away.\\n\\nAnxious voices of the Astronomical Bureau officials echoed through the corridors—the Curse of Jade Blood in Nong Chang had still not been rooted out, the last anchor point nowhere to be found. Nowhere to be found—yet in truth it was as far as the horizon and as near as his own eyes. Jin Xiao meant to laugh bitterly, but could only let out a hollow moan; he had fought his entire life, never imagining he himself would become the final poisoned chalice.\\n\\nJade Blood had once granted him boundless vitality—even pierced by a thousand arrows, even torn apart by blood-soaked halberds, even crushed beneath the beasts of the underworld! This withered frame had never once wavered! Now that all was settled, he could no longer face this bizarre ending with composure. This overflowing rage, this heart-rending resentment, this unfulfilled longing! The Curse of Jade Blood drifted up from the earth, rising into the sky, toward him—this body now bore the final crushing weight of the curse, yet also gathered the boundless power of Jade Blood within it. Why give up this endless life now! He felt blood surge once more through his withered bones, felt his jade shell crack, his limbs twist and contort. He fell to his knees with a thunderous crash, prostrating himself upon the earth, listening as his undying soul rejoiced at its rebirth—a yellowed letter slipped from between his shattered armor, falling to the ground with a thud, its crooked handwriting stained with blood and tears, reflected in his burning eyes. The [Jade Bone Immortal] buried his head gently among those words that would never return, letting the tears soak through this heavy weight of longing. His half-dead body seemed to recover its senses—the breeze brushed past, and this gentle touch felt so long unfelt, truly, so very long.\\n\\nThe drifting green figure propped himself up, pushed open the window, and let the moonlight illuminate himself. Feeling the cool wind against his face, he no longer heeded the shadows shrieking to stop him. He pictured the scenery of his homeland, imagined the man once called Jin Xiao standing beside his family as he once had. He thought and thought, until his thoughts finally stilled, until only a wash of moonlight remained beneath the window, shining down upon his distant homeland.

The Celestial Court's game is drawing to a close.\\n\\nThat capital official you once left behind now wears the brocade robes of an Imperial Censor, standing at the center of the great hall as the Celestial Court's voice echoes through it —\\n\\n『By decree of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Celestial Court: In this age when the very order of heaven and earth grows dim and the rule of law falters, this lord has set right what was wrong, achieved merit upon merit, holding steady one region with tireless labor. Across the realm, neither imperial kin nor provincial nobility can match such achievement — foremost among the dragons, acknowledged by court and commons alike. Let this one be elevated to Grand Guardian of the State, granted a thousand taels of gold and a hundred bolts of fine silk, proclaimed throughout the realm, that all may know of this extraordinary merit.』\\n\\nYou raise your head, silently regarding the capital official now transformed into an Imperial Censor. He holds the decree, head bowed slightly, wearing just the right smile — always that same false expression, always searching for some stain to make his mark upon. You already knew the Celestial Court had other designs, but never imagined they would stoop to such a shoddy scheme. These rewards and empty titles are worthless in themselves, yet more than enough to give others grounds for gossip, thrusting you into the eye of the storm, drawing every gaze and every arrow toward you alone. Now, in this age when Zhen Dan teeters on the brink of ruin, some still remain obsessed with political games — 'foremost among the dragons' — you cannot help but laugh aloud, wondering how those proud, competitive dragon-children will react upon reading this decree.\\n\\nThe Dragon Emperor has withdrawn from the world for a hundred years now, and the Celestial Court's seal no longer represents his will — the hundred offices of Wei Jing all hold their share of power, and among them, those who abuse borrowed authority to run rampant are everywhere.\\n\\nYu Zai has long since left the capital, and now there are precious few left in the Celestial Court capable of overturning this game.\\n\\nHe will be found.

War reports from Ling Nan have already reached the capital — the assault of the Serpent of Slaanesh has claimed nearly an entire generation of the Frontier Commandery's finest troops. The Wei Xi Provinces have held Khan Tamur's forces back west of Ashaash at the cost of blood, but plague knows no borders, and death marches ever closer to Shang Yang. Chaos Dwarf cannon fire has already shaken the very foundations of Chang Yuan. The great nation of Zhen Dan faces unprecedented challenge, the Celestial Empire is stretched to its limits, and each dragon alone cannot hope to withstand it all — we must strike back. The Celestial Court has issued a decree to the provinces, summoning all lords and nobles to the capital to deliberate matters of state.\\n\\nThis may appear to be a response to the crisis, but it is in truth merely another move in the game the Three Excellencies and Nine Ministers play to consolidate power. Wei Jing has long been a great whirlpool — everyone drawn into it eventually becomes a casualty of factional strife. And yet this is truly a rare opportunity to expand our influence — Zhen Dan's strength desperately needs to be unified, and before the scales settle, we should secure as much support as we can.

『My lord, your servants have, by imperial decree, thoroughly selected maidens of good family for the inner palace.\\nFrom the four directions the common folk converge upon this city, and its streets are filled with beauties.\\nThe eunuchs have made repeated selections, and secured six jade maidens.\\nWe know not if they will satisfy my lord's wishes — we beg my lord to inspect them personally before rendering judgment』

Calamity strikes without warning! Agents of Slaanesh have already infiltrated the inner palace, and within the city walls, numerous secret cults have risen in revolt! Some officers and soldiers have sunk into wine and lust, struck down by hidden assassins in the midst of their stupor; others, seduced by Slaanesh, have betrayed hearth and home to serve the enemy. Fortunately, a band of warriors still hold firm in their resolve, willing to give their lives for the Dragon Emperor! The most urgent task now is to reorganize our forces and establish defenses — this city is the foundation of our cause, and it must not fall into enemy hands!

Ye Sheng's methods are far from clever, but by selling out Zhen Dan's interests, he has indeed rallied enormous outside support — Skaven, Ogres, Hu tribesmen, truly a nest of snakes and rats! Their involvement has plunged the western provinces into chaos, and has pushed Zhao Ming's patience to its very limit. The mercenary warlords leading forces in the field have all received Bin Long's death order: march at once to Han Yu Port, rendezvous with the Eighth-Generation Lord, and then advance upon Shang Yang. All who dare obstruct their advance will be reduced to ash by the wrath of the divine dragon.

The great warship cleaves through the roiling waves of the sea — [Grand Admiral of Du Yuan] An Rui Bang's dragon-ship fleet has returned home, landing safely at Fu Zhou.\\n\\nThe righteous army's encampment erupts in thunderous cheers — this is the second Grand Admiral to return home in glory, and the Three Armies are inspired without exception. In days past he followed Yu Long deep into the misty rainforests of the Roselia continent, traversing untamed wildlands and enduring trials of life and death. Now, under Yuan Bo's decree, he has returned to his homeland bearing an ancient relic of the rainforest's foreign peoples. In the coming days he will erect an altar in Fu Zhou to perform a rite, using the power of this foreign treasure to reinforce the Five Elements Compass and strengthen its power of suppression.

He no longer bothers to hide his joy.\\n\\nThe relic of the ancient sages rests at the center of the great formation. An Rui Bang tries his best to appear pained, but the transcendent power surging into his body has already swept away his restraint. These ignorant mortals all see him as a hero, the crowds cheer his name, the Astronomers gather power at his command, and the Tide-Washing Court guards bow before him. The people watch with excitement as the power of the Winds of Magic converges and takes shape, anticipating that once the ritual is complete, this battered city will rise again.\\n\\nCracks spread through the golden filigree, and power accumulated over ten thousand years bursts forth, surging into the sky. The Astronomers strain under the shockwave, and the roaring gale whips at the Grand Admiral's sleeves as radiant light spills from the fissures in the relic, enveloping him. The people cheer at the dazzling halo that suddenly blooms in the heavens, paying no mind to the blue-robed figures darting through the crowd.\\n\\nAn Rui Bang's fingers have already begun to melt. He feels flesh sloughing away beneath his brocade robes, feathers sprouting, power swelling. 'My lord... is something wrong with the ritual? This power doesn't feel like the Moon Empress's... we...'\\n\\nThe relic of the ancient sages shatters completely in An Rui Bang's grip. The air twists and melts, flowing like liquid, and the flagstones of the ritual platform crack in unison. He looks upon the stunned, stupefied faces of the Astronomers before him, gives a soft click of the tongue between his beak, and lets demonic flame erupt from his talons, his voice warping amid the crackling of twisting flesh and blood. 'Thanks to all of you... for helping me ascend to immortality.'\\n\\nHis sinews coil and multiply like living things, wings burst forth from his back through splitting bone, and countless eyes of strange color open one after another across his warped shell.\\n\\nThe screaming faces of the Astronomers are burned to cinders in an instant, twisted into grotesque shapes, their fine robes and flesh fused into a single blazing torch, then scattered to ash by the pressure of beating wings.\\n\\nHow foolish — whether these mortals who live and die in a single day, or those dragons who have hesitated for tens of thousands of years.\\n\\nHe can finally trample them all beneath his feet.\\n\\nHe will bring enlightenment to this world.\\n\\nThe long blade cuts through the clamor of the marketplace, and thick smoke laced with sparks climbs into the sky, mingling with the fireworks still blooming overhead. The streets writhe and reshape themselves like living things, and buildings sprout eyes and mouths as they twist. The cheers of the city have changed their tune — the mad laughter of the Face-Painting Cult rings out, sweet to the ear. A strange, shifting halo collapses from the heavens like shattering glass, frozen against the night sky.\\n\\nAfter all these years, this noisy city has finally become a pleasure to behold — the work of Tzeentch is truly captivating.\\n\\nThe Greater Daemon hovering atop the observatory lowers its countless eyes, gazing down upon the city now transformed into a sea of fire and hell, and murmurs in satisfaction.\\n\\n'All for the Lord of All Change.'

Night rain patters against the stone paving of Fu Zhou — one night remains before the ritual begins.\\n\\nAn Rui Bang stands before the altar, hands clasped behind his back, fingers slowly stroking his beard. The relic of the ancient sages lies still at the center of the formation, faint light seeping through its gilded patterns. His brow furrows slightly, his expression heavy with concern for the nation and its people — this is the bearing he must show, the Grand Admiral of Du Yuan returning home in glory, a pillar of the state. Yet beneath his brocade robes, his Face-Painting Cult emblem burns hot with each heartbeat, ambition and rapture coursing through every limb. Only one night remains — endure this single night, and the glory of the Lord of All Change will descend upon this ruined city.\\n\\n'The Grand Admiral is in fine spirits, still rehearsing rituals so late at night.'\\n\\nA woman's voice rises behind him, light as a raindrop falling from the eaves in the night wind. An Rui Bang spins around abruptly. Zhao Qi leans against the altar's base, her plain white dress damp with night dew, her hair still dripping. Normally, this leader of the righteous army carries herself with gentle eyes and soft features, personally leading refugees, tending to the wounded and dying, the very picture of compassion and righteousness. But now the corner of her mouth curls in a half-smile, carrying an inexplicable, uncanny cunning.\\n\\n'Lady Zhao Qi, forgive my failure to receive you properly,' An Rui Bang says, suppressing the flutter in his heart, his expression outwardly composed. 'The ritual begins tomorrow — the fate of all of Fu Zhou's people hangs upon it. I dare not be lax.'\\n\\nZhao Qi walks slowly to the Grand Admiral's side, the tip of her shoe crushing fallen leaves underfoot, her gaze fixing directly on the relic at the formation's heart. She taps her own chin lightly with a fingertip. 'Lord An's return is well-timed indeed. Yet before this, you abandoned the people of He Dong to their suffering, leaving this mess behind — quite the difficulty for my righteous army to manage.'\\n\\nAn Rui Bang's pupils contract sharply, his fingers clenching tight. 'Lady Zhao, the calamity of the Dark Elves was, thankfully, quelled through the righteous army's great efforts. My departure from Fu Zhou was truly unavoidable. Now the four seas boil, chaos erupts on every side, and the four Grand Admirals each bear heavy burdens, stretched thin. Lord Yu Long set sail in search of a means to save the world from ruin, requiring my presence in Roselia. Now that Lord Yu Long's plans have entered a new stage, I too have returned bearing this divine relic, hoping only that it truly holds the power to protect the nation and its people.'\\n\\nZhao Qi brushes back a lock of hair, her eyes brimming with a seductive shimmer that momentarily entrances An Rui Bang. In the flickering firelight, he thinks he glimpses a fleeting, slit-pupiled shadow in the depths of her eyes. 'So it seems, Lord An and I are both simply people bound by circumstance beyond our control. Better, perhaps, to be common folk, free of such constraints, able to follow one's heart's desire.' The air in the hall seems to freeze solid. A cold glint flashes through An Rui Bang's eyes before he slowly sighs. 'My desires are no different from those of the righteous army — nothing more than peace and prosperity for the nation. As for you, Lady Zhao, having come all this way to safeguard the ritual, you too should rest soon.' Zhao Qi steps behind him, whispering softly. 'Is that truly all you desire?'\\n\\nIs this woman simply another who craves power, or does she have some other design? No — no, her words carry hidden edges, danger lurking in every phrase. Once tomorrow's ritual begins, all will be accomplished — but whatever she is scheming, tonight she must be permanently silenced.\\n\\n'If Lady Zhao is so inclined, why not join me at my humble quarters?' Zhao Qi's fingers rest lightly against his chest, her voice honeyed enough to drip. 'Then I shall trouble you to lead the way.'\\n\\nNow is the moment to act.\\n\\n'Lord An has quite refined taste,' Zhao Qi murmurs, her figure drifting slowly among the hanging paintings he has collected. An Rui Bang sits at the tea table, watching the moonlight cast Zhao Qi's ink-black shadow across the scrolls, along with the Face-Painting Cult assassins quietly closing in. He lifts his teacup gently, clinking it against the rim. 'A pastime to ease the heart. I have borne the name of prodigy since childhood, and in the forty-odd years since, I find the mysteries of heaven and earth ever more boundless, like standing before a vast ocean — a lifetime's effort could not reveal even one part in ten thousand. And yet — Lady Zhao, a thirst for knowledge burning too fiercely is rarely a good thing.' He closes his eyes to savor his tea, listening to the sound of blood spraying across the scrolls. 'Clean it all up — I must return to my preparations.'\\n\\n'No need to rush off.'\\n\\nAn Rui Bang's fingers tremble against the teacup. He snaps his head up — silver moonlight spills across Zhao Qi's shoulders, making her features all the more uncanny. The hanging paintings are now smeared with blood and shredded flesh, but the assassins' bodies have vanished without a trace.\\n\\nZhao Qi lifts aside a hanging painting, licking the blood from the corner of her mouth — those slit pupils belong to no human. 'I had thought the arts of Tzeentch prized subtlety and elegance of concept — I hadn't expected you'd exhaust yourself merely picking out an elegant place to die.' An Rui Bang stumbles to his feet, cold dread crawling up his spine. He draws his blade and forms a seal, needing two attempts before the pink flame catches, its eerie fire spreading through the scattered scrolls and casting monstrous shadows among the hanging paintings. Zhao Qi remains perfectly still, standing within the firelight, head tilted slightly, regarding her prey with amused interest. 'You monster — what, what exactly are you—' In the next instant, his vision lurches skyward, nine tails unfurling below him, sharp fangs tearing through his neck.\\n\\nHis lifeless eyes hang suspended in midair, slowly dimming.\\n\\n'To be called that again wounds me so — it has been thousands of years since anyone addressed me so. Since I now serve before the Moon Empress's throne, and the Xun-Wood direction lacks a guardian, I shall claim it for myself. From now on, call me Sovereign of the Green Hills — how does that sound?'

Agents of the God-Strategy Bureau have already brought news of the Fu Zhou incident back to the Celestial Court — one of the Four Grand Admirals, deeply trusted by Ming Long, has fallen to Chaos and launched a rebellion after returning from his expedition with Yu Long. This conspiracy runs deep and cannot be tolerated. Yun Feng Zi has repeatedly refused the capital's summons, and half of the Jade Sea Sovereign's fleet remains unaccounted for. With each dragon acting on their own, the Celestial Court's patience has worn thin. Yin Yin and Yuan Bo must both respond, or the Dragon Emperor's guard will come to find the answer themselves.
